issues.claim: Middlesex County's Office of Health Services states its goal is that every food establishment be inspected at least twice a year, by NJ-licensed Registered Environmental Health Specialists.
issues.problem: The cited county URL (and every variant path I tried on middlesexcountynj.gov) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, so I could not read the statement firsthand. Search results returning that page do quote 'at least twice a year' and 'New Jersey-licensed Registered Environmental Health Specialists', so the claim appears accurate but is not independently verified from an opened page.
issues.fix: Either cite a mirror/PDF of the county inspection page, or downgrade to 'county states a twice-yearly inspection goal (per search snippet; county page blocked to our crawler)' and note it in data_gaps.

issues.claim: DeltaTrak: 'Reusable BLE loggers roughly $199-$209 retail; single-use in-transit loggers about $6-$18 (reseller listing)' cited to https://solutionsprime.com/delivery-and-transportation/data-loggers
issues.problem: The cited category URL renders an empty catalogue ('0 products') with no prices in either readable or raw mode, so that URL does not support the figures. I did confirm $199.00 for the FlashLink 40902 BLE logger and $6.00/each for a 10-pack of FlashLink Mini in-transit loggers on other pages I opened at the same reseller; the upper ends ($209 and $18) were not individually seen.
issues.fix: Point the citation at the product pages actually showing the prices (40902 BLE detail page at $199.00; Mini in-transit 10-pack at $60.00 = $6.00 each) and drop or mark the unverified upper bounds, or record the range as 'about $199 and about $6 each, low end verified'.

issues.claim: measured_outcomes: low-cost open-hardware IoT node paper, sample = 'Single retail refrigerated cabinet deployment (proof of concept)'
issues.problem: The cited paper (Sensors 2020;20:846, PMC7038712) deployed four ESP8266 relay boards and ten DS18B20 probes across the refrigerated cabinets of one medium-sized store, not a single cabinet. The finding text is fine; only the sample description is imprecise.
issues.fix: Change sample to 'one medium-sized retail store, 4 ESP8266 nodes and 10 DS18B20 probes'.

issues.claim: measured_outcomes: 'Hotel group reports HACCP deviations falling from about one per week to about one per month' (Sensire case example, 2021)
issues.problem: The source is a single-property case study (Hotel Arthur, Finland), not a hotel group, and the page does not display a 2021 date (only the file name '11-21' suggests November 2021). The deviation numbers themselves are stated verbatim in the source.
issues.fix: Change 'Hotel group reports' to 'One hotel (Hotel Arthur) reports' and note the year as 'undated case study, file dated 11-2021'.

issues.claim: Two secondary-detail items in existing_solutions: Monnit 'iMonnit Basic free, Premiere paid annual' and Sensaphone 'WEB600 (6-zone)'.
issues.problem: Neither detail appears on the pages cited (the Monnit sensor page and the Absolute Automation SCD-1200 page). No price or outcome depends on them, but they are unsourced as written.
issues.fix: Cite the Monnit subscription page and the Sensaphone WEB600 page, or drop the plan names and the WEB600 zone count.

claims_checked.claim: FDA observed 397 retail deli departments in 2015-2016; 70.0% out of compliance on data item 5, 62.9% on data item 7 (cooling), 91.2% on improper holding/time-temperature overall

FDA 10-year trend study: in 2008 only 45% of full-service restaurants and 49% of delis were in compliance with improper holding/time-temperature; roughly 850 establishments observed per phase across nine facility types

NJ defines 'refrigeration temperatures' as 41 F or less, with a 45 F allowance only for equipment in use as of Jan 2, 2007, to be upgraded or replaced by Jan 2, 2012; potentially hazardous food must be held at refrigeration temperatures except during prep/cooking/cooling or approved time-as-control
N.J.A.C. 8:24-3.5(d)1 cooling is two-stage: within two hours from 135 F to 70 F, and within four hours from 70 F to refrigeration temperatures (i.e. sequential, up to six hours total)

Time as a public health control and specialized processes such as reduced-oxygen packaging require written procedures submitted to the health authority for approval and maintained on site (8:24-3.5(g)(4) and (h))

N.J.A.C. 8:24-2.1(b) requires at least one person in charge in Risk Type 3 establishments to be a certified food protection manager, and the person in charge must demonstrate HACCP knowledge at inspection
N.J.A.C. 8:24 was readopted effective November 17, 2021, and NJDOH's notice says rulemaking to conform to the newer federal Model Food Code is still in development
Middlesex County's Office of Health Services states a goal of inspecting every food establishment at least twice a year, by NJ-licensed Registered Environmental Health Specialists

USDA ERS 2005-06 supermarket loss averaged 11.4% fresh fruit, 9.7% fresh vegetables, 4.5% fresh meat/poultry/seafood; sample of six large national/regional retailers excluding convenience stores, megastores, club stores and mom-and-pop grocers; EIB-44, March 2009

ERS chart: loss rates for 24 fresh fruits from 4.1% (bananas) to 43.1% (papayas), from 2,900 US supermarkets in 2011-12; page attributes loss to culling misshapen/overstocked/spoiled product and does not mention refrigeration failure
A Lincoln, NE drive-through restaurant discarded about $1,800 of refrigerated product after an August 2024 storm outage and closed for a few days

Some commercial property policies include only a small amount of spoilage coverage; most carriers require a spoilage or utility service interruption endorsement; equipment breakdown coverage 'will pay to repair or replace the equipment that malfunctioned, but it will not cover the cost of spoiled inventory'

Middlesex County had 1,752 Accommodation and Food Services establishments employing 24,124 people in 2024 (7.0% of county establishments); Food Preparation and Serving Related employment projected 22,250 (2022) to 24,700 (2032)
TempGenius: a small install with fewer than five sensors costs approximately $2,000, and about 20 sensors about $5,000
Monnit ALTA temperature sensor MNS2-9-W2-TS-ST is $116.00; probe add-ons +$11 (3 ft) to +$117 (100 ft); 25-month NIST +$71 (8-point +$203); line power with battery backup +$50

ThermoWorks ThermaData WiFi Type K two-channel logger is $289.00 ($274 at 5+, $264 at 10+), meter only with probes sold separately, includes a 2-point NIST-traceable calibration certificate, stores 18,000 readings onboard
Adafruit pre-wired waterproof DS18B20 is $9.95 at 1-9 qty ($8.96 at 10-99) and includes the required 4.7k pull-up resistor
DeltaTrak FlashLink BLE reusable loggers about $199 retail and single-use in-transit loggers about $6 each, per the cited reseller listing

Sensaphone Sentinel SCD-1200 is a 12-zone panel, monitors its own power supply for failure, has 8-hour battery backup, and gates text and phone-call notifications behind a paid subscription; its price could not be read off any page opened (recorded as Unknown)
SmartSense's food-service page names Cafe Rio (155 locations), Wegmans, honeygrow, Sweetgreen and Lowes Foods
YOLO11s is 9.4M parameters, 47.0 mAP at 640px, 90.0 ms CPU ONNX and 2.5 ms on a T4
Liquid AI LFM2.5-VL ships in 450M, 1.6B and 3B variants, with the 450M positioned for edge deployment
Sensire case example: HACCP deviations down from about one per week to about one per month

Kelsius/Hastings Hotels: six hotels plus a gastro pub, each property saving about three hours per day for all food staff, and the same page states stock was lost 'due to no notifications of faulty appliances'

New Jersey is a one-party-consent state; intercepting an oral communication without a participant's consent is a third-degree crime under N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-3, with the one-party exception in 2A:156A-4(d); no NJ statute requires workplace camera signage; recording in restrooms/locker rooms is criminal under N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9

New Jersey Data Privacy Act effective January 15, 2025, applies to controllers processing 100,000+ consumers (25,000 if selling data), and treats biometric data as sensitive data requiring consent; FAQ page itself rendered only a bot-block interstitial
NJ requires the most recent inspection report on premises for public review for at least two years (8:24-8.13) and the evaluation placard posted near the public entrance (8:24-8.12)

2023 peer-reviewed cold-chain transport anomaly-detection study (Gillespie et al., Sustainability 15(3):2255) was a small trial on instrumented delivery vehicles, so transfer to a static walk-in is an inference
Low-cost open-source ESP-based IoT node gives continuous temperature visibility in retail refrigerated cabinets at parts cost far below commercial loggers, without demonstrating spoilage reduction
